lines.text: With regard to the facial nerve, which statement is true?
The answer is: it is secreto-motor to the lacrimal gland.
Meet the facial nerve, the seventh cranial nerve, smiling in the onion market.
Its branches spread across the face. It has a variety of different functions, and it is important clinically.
One branch runs up like a pipe. This is the greater petrosal nerve.
Through it, the facial nerve carries secreto-motor fibres to the lacrimal gland, and turns on the tap.
(laugh) And out flow the tears, onions or no onions.
Remember: the facial nerve is secreto-motor to the lacrimal gland, through the greater petrosal nerve.
Which one of the following statements concerning lung volumes is true?
The answer is: the vital capacity is the sum of the inspiratory reserve volume, the expiratory reserve volume, and the tidal volume.
The happy lung holds three balloons.
The red one is the inspiratory reserve volume, extra air you can still breathe in.
The blue one is the tidal volume, the air of a normal breath.
The yellow one is the expiratory reserve volume, extra air you can still breathe out.
Add the three together: that is the vital capacity, on the lung's sign.
The grumpy purple balloon is the residual volume. It stays out, so vital capacity is total lung capacity minus residual volume.
Remember: vital capacity equals inspiratory reserve, plus tidal volume, plus expiratory reserve.
The pathogenicity of the tubercle bacillus is primarily due to which one of the following?
The answer is a delayed hypersensitivity reaction against the bacteria.
Deep in the lung hides the green tubercle bacillus.
The T cells sound the alarm. Mycobacteria stimulate a specific T cell response of cell-mediated immunity.
They build a fortress around it: a granuloma, which reduces the infection.
The snail clock shows it is slow. This is delayed hypersensitivity, a type four reaction.
But the same T cells pour damage onto the lung tissue itself.
(sigh) So the damage comes mainly from the host's own immune response. This is called immune pathology.
Remember: the tubercle bacillus harms us mainly through our own delayed hypersensitivity reaction.
